data.description:
# rebar-debug must trace and record `caused_by` before it closes a bug

## Problem

The `rebar-debug` skill drives a bug to a proven, cited root cause — the strongest
evidence in the system about *which change* broke *what*. It then throws that
provenance away. Phase 1 ends with the mechanism, Phase 2 fixes it, and the ticket
closes without ever naming the ticket whose work introduced the defect.

rebar already has the machinery: `caused_by` is a first-class relation
(`graph/_links.py:CANONICAL_RELATIONS`), `rebar transition <bug> ... closed`
accepts `--caused-by=<id>` (`_commands/transition.py:65`), and the links feed
`rebar metrics`' escape-rate lenses plus the epic-close `caused_by` floor
(`docs/plan-review-gate.md:1091`). Absent an explicit `--caused-by`, a bug close
falls back to best-effort `git blame` auto-derivation over the ticket's impacted
paths, which blames *files* and records nothing when it cannot read them
(`docs/clone-guidance.md:13-19`).

So today the most rigorous debugging path in the repo feeds the weakest possible
input into the escape-rate metric: a file-level blame guess, or nothing. Defect
escape rate cannot be measured when the defects are not mapped to their origin.

## Plan

Amend `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` only. No code, no behavior change.

1. Add a required attribution step to Phase 1's exit gate (Stage 3), immediately
   before the RCA writeback: find the introducing change by blaming the *exact*
   lines the confirmed experiment implicated (not the file), walk through
   carriers (reformat/rename/move) to the commit that made the behavior wrong,
   recover the ticket from that commit's `rebar-ticket:` trailer or leading
   `<id>:` subject, and record it.
2. Route recording through the native surface — `--caused-by=<id>` on the bug
   close, paired with the matching `--class`; `rebar link <bug> <origin> caused_by`
   when the link is wanted earlier or the bug is already closed.
3. Hold attribution to the root cause's evidentiary standard, and enumerate the
   three resolutions: regression (attribute to the breaking change's ticket),
   omission (attribute by scope-of-work to the ticket that should have covered it),
   unattributable (record the searches that came up empty; leave the link unset).
   A fabricated origin is worse than none — it corrupts the metric it feeds.
4. Scope it to the `defect` / `incomplete-implementation` paths; the not-a-bug
   classifications have no defect to attribute.
5. Gate the close on it in "Reporting back", and add a **Defect origin** line to
   the report-back list.
6. Wire the supporting hooks: add the link to the approval-gate own-tracker
   carve-out (so it is pre-approved, not gated), note attribution retention on the
   fast path, and point Stage 1's git-history bullet at the exit-gate step.

## Acceptance criteria

- `SKILL.md` requires an origin ticket to be identified and recorded before the
  bug close, with the exact `--caused-by` syntax.
- The unattributable path is explicit and fails open to a recorded negative
  result, never to a guess.
- Attribution is scoped to defect / incomplete-implementation.
- The own-tracker approval carve-out lists the link, so recording it needs no
  user approval.
- `python3 scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` passes; no new >100-char lines.
data.title: rebar-debug: trace and record the defect's originating ticket (caused_by) before close
